stages.name: Foundations
stages.end: Read and write the Python and math the rest needs

units.title: Python for engineers
units.about: The Python a JavaScript developer needs to ship AI code: the language, environments, types, async and tests.

lessons.title: Python for a JavaScript developer
lessons.outcome: Read and write Python lists, dicts, comprehensions and functions, and avoid the traps that differ from JavaScript.
lessons.byHand: Predict the output of eight short snippets (integer division, truthiness of empty lists, a mutable default argument, copying a list) before running any of them.

lessons.title: Virtual environments and packaging
lessons.outcome: Create an isolated environment, pin dependencies, and turn a script into an installable package with a pyproject.toml.
lessons.byHand: Compare two recorded dependency lists from a laptop and a server and find the one version difference that breaks the import.

lessons.title: Type hints, dataclasses and Pydantic
lessons.outcome: Annotate functions, model records as dataclasses and Pydantic models, read checker and validation errors, and decide where types pay off.
lessons.byHand: Annotate a function that parses a sensor reading, then predict which of six calls mypy flags and which of four raw payloads Pydantic rejects.

lessons.title: async and await in Python
lessons.outcome: Run several slow calls at the same time with asyncio and tell when async helps and when it does not.
lessons.byHand: Drag three call bars (2 s, 1 s, 3 s) onto a timeline, first awaited one after another and then together, and enter both predicted total times.

lessons.title: Testing with pytest
lessons.outcome: Write unit tests with fixtures and parametrized cases, and read a failing test report to find the bug.
lessons.byHand: Write the expected output for five inputs to a text-splitting function by hand, then diagnose a recorded failing test report.

units.title: NumPy and pandas
units.about: Work with numbers in whole arrays and tables at once, and clean the messy data real projects start with.

lessons.title: NumPy arrays, shapes and vectorized maths
lessons.outcome: Replace Python loops with array operations and predict the shape of every result.
lessons.byHand: Fill in the row and column totals of a 4-by-7 grid of daily step counts cell by cell, then predict the shapes that summing by rows and by columns give.

lessons.title: Broadcasting and shape errors
lessons.outcome: Predict when two arrays of different shapes combine, and fix a shape error from its message.
lessons.byHand: For six pairs of shapes, say whether they broadcast and what shape comes out, then diagnose a recorded shape error.

lessons.title: pandas DataFrames: load, filter, group
lessons.outcome: Load a CSV into a DataFrame, filter rows, and group and aggregate to answer a question.
lessons.byHand: Sort the 12 rows of an on-page taxi trip log into pickup districts by dragging, then type the average fare for each district.

lessons.title: Cleaning messy data with pandas
lessons.outcome: Find and fix missing values, wrong types, duplicates and bad joins before the data reaches a model.
lessons.byHand: Click every problem cell in a recorded 15-row patient CSV (blank cells, 'N/A', a duplicated id, dates stored as text) and label it before writing code.

units.title: Vectors, matrices and slopes
units.about: The linear algebra and calculus models run on, drawn as arrows, grids and hills instead of formulas.

lessons.title: Vectors as arrows and as lists of features
lessons.outcome: Describe things as vectors of features and compute the distance between two of them.
lessons.byHand: Drag five running shoes onto a grid by weight and cushioning, then pick which two are closest and type their distance.

lessons.title: The dot product and cosine similarity
lessons.outcome: Compute a dot product and cosine similarity and explain why vector length can mislead a similarity score.
lessons.byHand: Fill in the dot-product scores of three films against a viewer's taste vector, rank them, then rank again with cosine and spot what changed.

lessons.title: Matrices as many dot products at once
lessons.outcome: Multiply a matrix by a vector or another matrix, read it as a transform, and fix mismatched shapes.
lessons.byHand: Drag the corners of a square to where a 2-by-2 matrix sends them, then fill in a bakery's order bill as a price matrix times a quantity vector.

lessons.title: Derivatives as slopes
lessons.outcome: Estimate a derivative by nudging the input a little and explain what its sign and size say.
lessons.byHand: Read a recorded fuel-use curve against driving speed and estimate the slope at three speeds by nudging the speed by 1 km/h.

lessons.title: Gradients and the chain rule
lessons.outcome: Compute a two-input gradient numerically, read which way is downhill, and chain slopes through nested functions.
lessons.byHand: On a contour map, nudge each of two inputs and pick the downhill arrow, then multiply two recorded slopes (heater to air temperature, air temperature to growth) and predict the combined slope.

units.title: Probability and what a model is
units.about: Reason about uncertainty with counts, distributions and Bayes, then see what a model actually is.

lessons.title: Distributions, mean and spread from counts
lessons.outcome: Turn recorded observations into a distribution, read probabilities and spread from it, and choose mean or median to summarise it.
lessons.byHand: Drop 40 recorded lift waits into histogram bins for two lift banks, read the chance of waiting over two minutes, and pick the more reliable bank from mean, median and spread.

lessons.title: Conditional probability and Bayes' rule
lessons.outcome: Update a belief with new evidence using Bayes' rule and avoid ignoring the base rate.
lessons.byHand: On a grid of 1,000 tiles standing for bags, click to colour the ones holding a banned item and the ones that set off the alarm, then type the chance an alarmed bag really holds one.

lessons.title: What a model is: a function with tuned numbers
lessons.outcome: Explain a model as a function with parameters fitted to data and spot the inputs where it should not be trusted.
lessons.byHand: Drag a line by eye through recorded daily sales against temperature, predict two new days, and mark the regions (heatwaves, holidays) where the line breaks down.

stages.name: Classic ML
stages.end: Train, evaluate and debug a model on tabular data

units.title: Fitting a line and a boundary
units.about: How a model learns: measure how wrong it is, then nudge its numbers downhill until it is less wrong.

lessons.title: Loss: one number for how wrong a model is
lessons.outcome: Compute mean squared error for any guessed line and say which of two lines fits better.
lessons.byHand: Drag a straight line through eight recorded days of sales, fill in each miss, square and average them, then try to beat your own score.

lessons.title: Gradient descent: walking downhill on the loss
lessons.outcome: Run gradient descent for a few steps, predict whether the next step lowers the loss, and spot a step size that is too big or too small.
lessons.byHand: From a starting slope, fill in the gradient and the loss after each of three fixed-size steps, then predict what a step ten times larger does to the loss.

lessons.title: Linear regression from scratch, then in scikit-learn
lessons.outcome: Write a NumPy linear regression with several inputs and check its weights against scikit-learn's.
lessons.byHand: Predict which of three inputs (weight, distance, volume) gets the largest weight, then compare your ranking with the fitted numbers.

lessons.title: Logistic regression: a probability instead of a number
lessons.outcome: Turn a weighted sum into a probability with the sigmoid, explain why log loss punishes confident mistakes, and say when a straight boundary or a widest-margin SVM falls short.
lessons.byHand: For five past applications, fill in the probability for each given score and the log loss of a confident wrong answer against a cautious one.

units.title: Honest evaluation
units.about: Keep the test fair: split the data properly, spot leaks, and notice when a model memorises instead of learns.

lessons.title: Train, validation and test sets, and cross-validation
lessons.outcome: Split a dataset three ways, run k-fold cross-validation, and say which score to report.
lessons.byHand: Drag twenty labelled rows into five folds, then mark for each fold which rows it trains on and which it is scored on.

lessons.title: Data leakage: when the model sees the answer
lessons.outcome: Find the leaking column or step in a pipeline that scores too well and rebuild it so it cannot leak.
lessons.byHand: Inspect a recorded feature list and evaluation with 99% accuracy and mark the column that is only known after the outcome.

lessons.title: Overfitting and regularization
lessons.outcome: Read a train-versus-validation gap, add an L2 or L1 penalty from scratch, and pick its strength by validation.
lessons.byHand: Predict which of three fitted curves (straight, gentle, wiggly) wins on new points, then fill in the penalised loss for one set of weights.

units.title: Metrics and choosing one
units.about: Accuracy hides a lot. Count the kinds of mistakes, trade them off with a threshold, and handle rare classes.

lessons.title: Confusion matrix, precision, recall and F1
lessons.outcome: Build a confusion matrix from predictions and choose precision or recall from the cost of each mistake.
lessons.byHand: Drag twenty flagged and unflagged messages into the four boxes, then fill in precision, recall and F1 yourself.

lessons.title: Thresholds, ROC and precision-recall curves
lessons.outcome: Move a decision threshold, read ROC and precision-recall curves, and pick an operating point for a stated cost.
lessons.byHand: Slide the threshold over ten scored cases, fill in true and false positive rates at each stop, and place the points on the chart.

lessons.title: Imbalanced data: when the thing you want is rare
lessons.outcome: Spot a useless high-accuracy model and fix it with class weights, resampling or a better metric.
lessons.byHand: Score a model that always says 'not fraud' on a recorded set with 0.5% fraud and diagnose why its accuracy looks great.

units.title: Trees, forests and boosting
units.about: Models that ask yes-or-no questions, then many of them voting or correcting each other: the workhorses of tabular data.

lessons.title: Decision trees: choosing the best question
lessons.outcome: Pick a tree split by computing Gini impurity and explain why a deep tree overfits.
lessons.byHand: For twelve members, fill in the Gini impurity of two candidate splits and choose the first question of the tree.

lessons.title: Random forests: many trees voting
lessons.outcome: Train a random forest, compare it with one tree on validation, and read its feature importances with caution.
lessons.byHand: Given three bootstrap samples of ten rows, fill in each small tree's vote for a new member and the majority result.

lessons.title: Gradient boosting: each tree fixes the last one's errors
lessons.outcome: Explain boosting as fitting residuals, train a boosted model, and stop it early before it overfits.
lessons.byHand: Choose the split for two one-split stumps in turn, each fitted to the leftover errors of the one before, and fill in the residuals after each.

units.title: More models, with and without labels
units.about: Neighbours and word counts with labels, then finding groups and squeezing many columns into a few without them.

lessons.title: k-nearest neighbours and why scale matters
lessons.outcome: Classify by nearest neighbours, choose k by validation, and show how unscaled features break distances.
lessons.byHand: Fill in distances from a new seedling to six labelled ones, vote with k=3, then redo it after the height column changes from centimetres to millimetres.

lessons.title: Naive Bayes for text: counting words
lessons.outcome: Score a review with naive Bayes from word counts and explain what the 'naive' assumption gives up.
lessons.byHand: From a table of word counts in bug reports and other reviews, multiply the probabilities for a new review and choose its label.

lessons.title: Clustering with k-means
lessons.outcome: Run k-means by hand for two rounds, choose k from an elbow plot, and recognise when clusters are not real.
lessons.byHand: Drag ten points to the nearest of two centres, fill in each group's average as the new centre, and repeat once.

lessons.title: Dimensionality reduction with PCA
lessons.outcome: Project data onto its main directions with PCA, read the explained variance, and use it to plot many columns in two.
lessons.byHand: Drag a line along the direction a cloud of two correlated sensor readings spreads most, then predict where each point lands when projected onto it.

units.title: Feature preparation and pipelines
units.about: Turn messy columns into model inputs and wrap every step in one pipeline that cannot leak.

lessons.title: Feature preparation: missing values, categories, scaling
lessons.outcome: Choose imputation, encoding and scaling for each column type and justify each choice.
lessons.byHand: Go through a recorded table of job candidates column by column and choose the treatment each needs (fill, one-hot, scale, drop).

lessons.title: scikit-learn pipelines from raw table to model
lessons.outcome: Build a Pipeline with a ColumnTransformer, tune it with cross-validation, and prove it does not leak.
lessons.byHand: Find the bug in a recorded script that scales the whole dataset before splitting, then predict how its score changes once fixed.

stages.name: Deep learning
stages.end: Write a training loop in PyTorch and explain backpropagation

units.title: Neurons and backpropagation
units.about: What one neuron computes, how layers pass numbers forward, and how blame flows back to every weight.

lessons.title: The neuron: weighted sum plus a bend
lessons.outcome: Compute a single neuron's output by hand and explain why it needs a non-linear activation.
lessons.byHand: Fill in the weighted sum and ReLU output for five readings in an in-page table, then predict whether two stacked linear neurons can draw the curved boundary shown, before the plot answers.

lessons.title: Forward pass through a small network
lessons.outcome: Trace a 2-3-1 network's forward pass as matrix products and predict each layer's shape.
lessons.byHand: Fill in the three hidden-layer cells for one input, then type the shape of every matrix and bias before running the NumPy version.

lessons.title: Backpropagation by hand on a tiny network
lessons.outcome: Apply the chain rule to get every weight's gradient in a two-layer network and check one numerically.
lessons.byHand: Push one wrong prediction backward through a 2-2-1 network by filling each local slope into the page's graph, then nudge one weight by 0.001 and enter the loss change to confirm your gradient.

lessons.title: Train a three-class network from scratch
lessons.outcome: Write forward, backward and update steps in NumPy with a softmax and cross-entropy output, train it on three tangled classes, and compare with scikit-learn's MLPClassifier.
lessons.byHand: Compute softmax probabilities and the cross-entropy for one sample from three scores, then predict whether the loss will fall, stall or explode for three learning rates and explain the one you got wrong.

units.title: PyTorch and the training loop
units.about: The same network rebuilt with PyTorch tensors, autograd, a standard training loop and real optimizers.

lessons.title: What PyTorch tensors add to NumPy arrays
lessons.outcome: Pick tensor dtypes and devices, choose view or reshape, and fix dtype and contiguity errors from their messages.
lessons.byHand: Predict the result dtype of six mixed operations and which of four view calls will fail after a transpose, then diagnose three recorded error messages.

lessons.title: Autograd: let PyTorch do the backward pass
lessons.outcome: Use requires_grad and backward() to get gradients and check them against your hand-derived ones.
lessons.byHand: Type the gradients you expect from your earlier hand calculation, then compare with autograd and predict what calling backward twice does to them.

lessons.title: The training loop, line by line
lessons.outcome: Write a PyTorch loop with batches, zero_grad, backward, step and a validation pass, and say what each line is for.
lessons.byHand: Drag eight shuffled loop lines into the right order, then pick which missing line explains a recorded run whose loss never moves.

lessons.title: Optimizers: SGD, momentum and Adam
lessons.outcome: Choose an optimizer and learning rate for a task and explain what momentum and Adam change about a step.
lessons.byHand: Click out five steps across an in-page loss surface with plain SGD and with momentum, then predict which reaches the minimum first in the recorded run.

units.title: Making training work
units.about: Starting weights, layer normalization, regularization and reading loss curves to find out why a run fails.

lessons.title: Weight initialization and why zeros fail
lessons.outcome: Explain why all-zero or too-large starting weights break training and pick a sensible default.
lessons.byHand: Predict the activation spread at layer ten of a ten-layer net for three starting scales (shrink, explode or stay healthy, plus a rough number), then run it and compare.

lessons.title: Batch norm against layer norm
lessons.outcome: Add batch or layer normalization to a network, say which one suits tiny batches, and avoid the train-versus-eval trap.
lessons.byHand: Compute batch-norm outputs for a batch of two values and for a batch of one, predict what happens to each, then choose batch or layer norm for three training setups.

lessons.title: Dropout, weight decay and early stopping
lessons.outcome: Add dropout, weight decay and early stopping to a model that overfits, and remember to switch to eval mode.
lessons.byHand: Mark the epoch where you would stop on a recorded overfitting curve, then predict how validation accuracy changes with dropout on versus off at test time.

lessons.title: Debugging a run from its loss curves
lessons.outcome: Diagnose underfitting, overfitting, a too-high learning rate and a data bug from curves, then apply a fixed checklist to find the cause.
lessons.byHand: Match four recorded curve pairs to their causes, then work a broken run through the checklist (one-batch test, label histogram, gradient-norm log) and name the bug before seeing the fix.

units.title: Convnets, embeddings, GPUs, Keras
units.about: Networks that see local patterns, vectors that stand for things, running on a GPU, and reading Keras code.

lessons.title: Convolutional networks in brief
lessons.outcome: Slide a filter over an image grid by hand and explain why a convnet needs far fewer weights than a dense layer.
lessons.byHand: Fill in the output cells of a 3x3 edge filter over a 6x6 grid of pixel numbers, and type the output size with and without padding.

lessons.title: Embeddings: learned vectors for categories
lessons.outcome: Replace one-hot columns with an nn.Embedding layer and read similarity off the trained vectors.
lessons.byHand: Enter how many weights a one-hot encoding of 5,000 ingredient ids costs against a 16-number embedding, then pick which ingredients you expect to end up close after training.

lessons.title: GPUs and why they matter
lessons.outcome: Move a model and its batches to a GPU, measure the speedup, and fix a device-mismatch error.
lessons.byHand: Estimate the multiply-adds in one training step of a given network, then compare your guess with recorded CPU and free-Colab GPU timings.

lessons.title: Reading Keras and TensorFlow code
lessons.outcome: Translate a Keras model and its compile and fit calls into the matching PyTorch pieces.
lessons.byHand: Match each line of a short Keras script to its PyTorch equivalent, then pick the line that explains why its recorded validation loss differs.

units.title: Computer vision, briefly
units.about: Reusing a trained image model on a small dataset, and choosing the right vision task for a product need.

lessons.title: Transfer learning for a small image dataset
lessons.outcome: Fine-tune a pretrained image model by freezing layers, replacing the head and adding safe augmentations.
lessons.byHand: Choose which layers to freeze for three dataset sizes and which of six augmentations are safe, then find the colour jitter that erased the disease's yellowing in a recorded run.

lessons.title: Classification, detection and segmentation
lessons.outcome: Choose between classification, detection and segmentation for a product need, or a hosted vision model instead.
lessons.byHand: Label four product requests with the vision task they need and draw on a sample photo the output each one returns.

units.title: Reinforcement learning, briefly
units.about: Learning from rewards instead of labels: the agent loop, a tiny Q-table, and where RL is actually used.

lessons.title: Rewards, states and a tiny Q-table
lessons.outcome: Fill in a Q-table by hand for a small grid task and train it with tabular Q-learning in NumPy.
lessons.byHand: Update four Q-table cells after a short recorded episode, then predict the route the agent takes once training ends.

lessons.title: Where RL is used, and where it is not
lessons.outcome: Run a standard RL environment and judge whether a business problem needs RL or plain supervised learning.
lessons.byHand: Sort six product ideas into RL, supervised learning or simple rules, then mark the point on a recorded reward curve where the agent starts gaming its reward.

stages.name: NLP
stages.end: Build a tiny GPT, fine-tune a BERT-style model

units.title: Turning text into numbers
units.about: How raw text becomes tokens, counts and vectors a model can use, and where each method breaks.

lessons.title: Tokens and byte-pair encoding by hand
lessons.outcome: Build a byte-pair encoding vocabulary from a small corpus and split an unseen word with it.
lessons.byHand: Click the most frequent adjacent character pair in twelve ferry departure notices, watch it merge, repeat five merges, then type how the page will split 'redeparting' before running the code.

lessons.title: Korean and Uzbek in a real tokenizer
lessons.outcome: Diagnose why Korean and Uzbek text costs more tokens and splits badly, and choose a fix or a different tokenizer.
lessons.byHand: Enter your predicted token count for one sentence in English, Korean and Uzbek (Latin and Cyrillic), compare with recorded tokenizer output, and select the splits that cut through meaning.

lessons.title: Bag of words: counting instead of reading
lessons.outcome: Turn a set of short texts into a word-count matrix and say what the matrix loses.
lessons.byHand: Fill the count cells for six job-board vacancy ads, then pick the two ads with opposite meaning that end up with identical rows.

lessons.title: TF-IDF: weighting words that are rare elsewhere
lessons.outcome: Compute TF-IDF weights, rank documents for a query, check against scikit-learn, and name BM25 as the variant search engines use.
lessons.byHand: Enter the weight of 'meter' and 'the' across eight customer emails, then predict which email ranks first for the query 'double charged meter'.

lessons.title: Train a tiny word2vec and find neighbours
lessons.outcome: Train skip-gram word vectors with NumPy, look up a word's nearest neighbours by cosine, and explain why shared contexts pull words together.
lessons.byHand: List the context-window pairs for two rider messages by dragging words into pairs, then predict which two place names will end up nearest neighbours after training.

units.title: Models that read in order
units.about: Predicting the next word from the ones before: counting n-grams, then recurrent networks and their limits.

lessons.title: N-gram language models and perplexity
lessons.outcome: Build a bigram model with smoothing, sample text from it, and measure it with perplexity on held-out sentences.
lessons.byHand: Fill a word-pair count table from fifteen weather-report sentences, choose the likeliest word after 'heavy', and predict the probability of a sentence with an unseen pair before smoothing.

lessons.title: Recurrent networks: one hidden state carried along
lessons.outcome: Run a recurrent network's forward pass step by step and explain what the hidden state stores.
lessons.byHand: Enter the hidden state after each of four steps through a two-unit recurrent cell with given weights, then check your cells against the NumPy run.

lessons.title: Vanishing gradients in recurrent networks
lessons.outcome: Diagnose vanishing and exploding gradients from recorded per-step gradient norms and fix the exploding case with gradient clipping.
lessons.byHand: Predict the gradient size after twenty steps for factors 0.8 and 1.2, then choose a clipping threshold that keeps a recorded norm series bounded without flattening it.

lessons.title: LSTM and GRU: gates that decide what to keep
lessons.outcome: Train an LSTM and a GRU on the same sequence task in PyTorch and explain how gates keep long-range information.
lessons.byHand: Set the forget, input and output gate sliders for a toy sequence so the cell still remembers a bracket opened eight steps earlier.

lessons.title: Sequence-to-sequence and its bottleneck
lessons.outcome: Explain encoder-decoder translation and show from recorded results why one fixed-size vector fails on long inputs.
lessons.byHand: Pick three numbers to encode a twelve-word sentence, let the page decode from them and mark the words that came back wrong, then predict where a recorded score-by-length chart drops.

units.title: Attention and transformers
units.about: Attention built by hand, then a transformer block, then a tiny GPT trained in a notebook.

lessons.title: Attention by hand: weighted lookups
lessons.outcome: Compute attention scores, softmax weights and the weighted sum for one query, and explain how it removes the bottleneck.
lessons.byHand: Enter the dot-product score of four keys against one query, turn them into weights, and fill in the blended value before checking with NumPy.

lessons.title: Self-attention, multiple heads and the causal mask
lessons.outcome: Write scaled dot-product self-attention with a causal mask and several heads (split, attend, concatenate) in NumPy, and spot a mask that leaks.
lessons.byHand: Click the cells of a five-by-five attention grid a next-word model must not see, predict what breaks if one stays open, then enter the shapes after splitting into two heads.

lessons.title: Positional encoding: telling word order apart
lessons.outcome: Show that self-attention ignores order, add sinusoidal or learned position vectors, and compare the outputs.
lessons.byHand: Shuffle the words of 'dog bites man' and predict whether plain self-attention outputs change, then add position vectors and predict again.

lessons.title: A transformer block from scratch
lessons.outcome: Assemble multi-head attention, a feed-forward layer, residual connections and layer norm into one working block in PyTorch.
lessons.byHand: Fill in the tensor shape after every layer of the block, then pick the line in a recorded broken block where the shapes stop matching.

lessons.title: Build, train and sample a tiny GPT
lessons.outcome: Stack transformer blocks into a character-level GPT, train it, sample with temperature, and decide when a small model is enough.
lessons.byHand: Enter the starting loss you expect from the vocabulary size, then match three recorded sample sets to the temperature that produced each.

units.title: Pretrained models at work
units.about: Using and fine-tuning BERT-style models for real tasks, and measuring the results honestly.

lessons.title: BERT against GPT: reading versus writing
lessons.outcome: Explain masked versus next-token training and pick an encoder or a decoder model for a given task.
lessons.byHand: Fill masked words in five sentences seeing both sides of the gap, then again seeing only the left side, and sort ten product tasks into encoder or decoder.

lessons.title: Fine-tune BERT for classification
lessons.outcome: Fine-tune a small BERT-style model for text classification with Hugging Face on a free Colab GPU and fix common setup errors.
lessons.byHand: Label twenty helpdesk tickets yourself, then read a recorded failed run (wrong label count, flat loss) and choose the cause before running the notebook.

lessons.title: Entity extraction with BIO tags
lessons.outcome: Tag entities with the BIO scheme, run a token-classification model, and repair labels broken by subword splits.
lessons.byHand: Tag the names, dates and amounts in six bank-transfer notes with B, I and O, then align your tags to the subword tokens a tokenizer produced.

lessons.title: Scoring NLP output: span F1, BLEU and ROUGE
lessons.outcome: Compute entity-level span F1, BLEU and ROUGE from scratch and choose the metric that matches the task.
lessons.byHand: Score a recorded set of entity spans and three machine summaries, then pick the summary that scores highest on ROUGE but states a wrong fact.

stages.name: LLM engineering
stages.end: Build RAG and agent systems and prove they work

units.title: Inside the model
units.about: What a chat model receives and returns: tokens in a fixed window, a weighted pick per token, and training that made it a chat model.

lessons.title: Tokens and the context window as a budget
lessons.outcome: Count the tokens in a request with a model's own tokenizer and predict when long input gets cut off or leaves no room for the answer.
lessons.byHand: For five recorded requests with their printed token counts, fill in input plus expected answer length and mark which ones overflow a small window and where the cut lands.

lessons.title: Temperature, top-p and how the next token is picked
lessons.outcome: Turn a model's scores into probabilities, sample from them with temperature and top-p, and choose settings for a given task.
lessons.byHand: Given recorded next-token scores for one sentence, rank the candidates, predict which ones survive a top-p cut, then predict how temperature changes the spread.

lessons.title: From next-token model to chat assistant
lessons.outcome: Explain how pretraining, instruction tuning and preference tuning turn a text predictor into an assistant, and write a messages request in the chat template it expects.
lessons.byHand: Match four recorded replies to the same question with the model stage that produced them (base, instruction-tuned, preference-tuned), then fill a chat template by placing system, user and assistant turns in order.

lessons.title: Why models make things up
lessons.outcome: Diagnose a confident wrong answer as missing knowledge, a bad prompt, or sampling, and pick the matching fix.
lessons.byHand: Sort ten recorded answers from a small open model about a museum's exhibitions into correct, invented, or outdated, and mark what the model could not have known.

units.title: Prompting
units.about: Writing instructions a model follows reliably: clear structure, examples, room to reason, machine-readable output and reusable prefixes.

lessons.title: Structure of a prompt: role, task, data, format
lessons.outcome: Rewrite a vague prompt into separated instructions, input data and output format, and explain why each part is there.
lessons.byHand: Take a recorded prompt that keeps producing the wrong summaries, label each sentence as instruction, data or format, and find the line the model obeyed by mistake.

lessons.title: Few-shot examples and how to pick them
lessons.outcome: Choose a handful of examples for a prompt by similarity and balance, and spot when examples bias the answers.
lessons.byHand: From twenty labelled plumbing job requests, pick three examples for a new request, then predict the label a recorded model gave with a lopsided example set.

lessons.title: Asking for reasoning steps, and what it costs
lessons.outcome: Decide when to ask a model to work step by step, and weigh the accuracy gain against extra tokens and time.
lessons.byHand: Compare recorded runs with and without step-by-step reasoning on twelve fare questions, count which got better, which got worse and how many extra tokens each used.

lessons.title: Reasoning models and the effort setting
lessons.outcome: Explain what a reasoning model does with hidden thinking tokens, set its effort or thinking budget for a task, and weigh the accuracy gain against cost and waiting time.
lessons.byHand: For six recorded tasks run at low and high effort (a date question, a lookup, a multi-step schedule puzzle, a rewrite, a maths word problem, a classification), predict which ones high effort actually helps, then compare with the recorded answers, token counts and times.

lessons.title: Structured output: getting valid JSON back
lessons.outcome: Define an output schema, validate model replies against it, and recover when a reply breaks the schema.
lessons.byHand: Check eight recorded model replies against a job-card schema, mark each one valid or broken and name exactly which field fails.

lessons.title: Prompt caching: putting the stable part first
lessons.outcome: Reorder a prompt so its unchanging prefix can be reused across calls, and read usage numbers to confirm the cache was hit.
lessons.byHand: Mark which parts of a recorded permit-help prompt change per question, reorder it so the fixed part comes first, and predict from recorded usage logs which calls reused the prefix.

units.title: Tool use
units.about: Letting a model ask your code to do things: the call-execute-reply loop, and exposing tools to many apps through MCP.

lessons.title: Function calling: the request and reply loop
lessons.outcome: Write the loop that reads a model's tool request, runs the function, sends the result back and stops at the final answer.
lessons.byHand: Play the app's part on a recorded transcript: read each tool request from the model, look up the answer in a printed session table, and fill in the reply message it needs.

lessons.title: MCP servers: sharing tools across apps
lessons.outcome: Build a small MCP server that exposes a tool and a resource, connect it to a client, and judge when a plain function call is enough.
lessons.byHand: Read a recorded MCP session log between a client and a seat-inventory server, label each message as discovery, call or result, and find the call that failed and why.

units.title: Embeddings and search
units.about: Finding the right passages fast: chunking, sentence embeddings, vector indexes, keyword plus meaning search, filters and reranking.

lessons.title: Chunking documents for search
lessons.outcome: Split documents into chunks by size, overlap or structure, and diagnose an answer that failed because the fact was cut in half.
lessons.byHand: Drag chunk boundaries over a recorded safety manual at a given size, then find which chunking splits the refuelling-distance rule across two chunks.

lessons.title: Embedding models: from word vectors to sentences
lessons.outcome: Explain how a bi-encoder pools token vectors into one sentence vector, and choose a multilingual model for Korean by testing it on your own queries.
lessons.byHand: Mean-pool four recorded token vectors into one sentence vector, then mark the top-3 results two recorded models returned for ten Korean and English queries as relevant or not and count hits.

lessons.title: Vector indexes: exact search against fast search
lessons.outcome: Build brute-force nearest-neighbour search and a simple clustered index, trade recall against speed, and say when a vector database beats an in-memory index.
lessons.byHand: Place twelve recorded 2-D product vectors on a grid, pick the three nearest to a query, then predict which one a clustered index misses because it sits in the next cluster.

lessons.title: Hybrid search: keywords, meaning and filters
lessons.outcome: Fuse a BM25 ranking and a vector ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, apply a metadata filter, and tell which queries each ranker wins alone.
lessons.byHand: Given two recorded ranked lists for serial-number and plain-description queries, drop the rows the branch filter excludes, fuse the rest with rank fusion and predict the new top three.

lessons.title: Rerankers and cross-encoders
lessons.outcome: Add a cross-encoder reranking step after retrieval and decide how many candidates it should rerank for the time you have.
lessons.byHand: Reorder a recorded top-ten retrieval for a plant-care question by reading each passage, then compare your order with recorded bi-encoder scores and cross-encoder scores.

units.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
units.about: Answering from your own documents: the pipeline from scratch, rewritten and repeated queries, citations and graphs.

lessons.title: A RAG pipeline from scratch
lessons.outcome: Build retrieve, assemble and answer steps on precomputed vectors without a framework, then rebuild the same pipeline in LangChain and map each step.
lessons.byHand: For three recorded member questions, pick the chunks you would retrieve from a coworking handbook, fill in the prompt you would send, and compare with the recorded pipeline's choices.

lessons.title: Rewriting queries and retrieving in rounds
lessons.outcome: Turn follow-ups into standalone queries, and write a retrieve-check-retrieve loop with a stop rule for questions that need two facts.
lessons.byHand: Rewrite three recorded follow-ups ('and the one after lunch?') into standalone queries and mark which recorded retrievals they turn from miss to hit, then trace one two-hop question through the programme.

lessons.title: Citations that point to real chunks
lessons.outcome: Make answers cite chunk ids in a fixed format, and reject or repair citations that do not resolve to a retrieved chunk.
lessons.byHand: Go through a recorded answer with citations and, for each marker, choose whether it resolves to a retrieved chunk, names a chunk that was never retrieved, or is malformed.

lessons.title: Graph-based RAG: entities and relations
lessons.outcome: Build a small entity-relation graph from extracted facts, answer a relationship question by walking it, and judge when plain vector RAG is enough.
lessons.byHand: Connect twenty recorded extracted facts about a film festival's films, directors and venues into a graph, then answer two relationship questions by following edges.

lessons.title: Questions over tables: text-to-SQL and a semantic layer
lessons.outcome: Answer a plain-language question over a relational database by having a model write SQL against a described schema, check the query before running it, and explain why a semantic layer of named metrics beats raw schemas.
lessons.byHand: Given a four-table schema and five recorded model-written queries, find the two that run but return wrong numbers (a join that double-counts, a missing date filter), then define one metric in a tiny semantic layer and see the model reuse it.

lessons.title: Keeping retrieval data fresh: updates, deletes and re-embedding
lessons.outcome: Keep a search index in step with its source documents by ingesting only what changed, removing deleted documents, and planning a full re-embed when the embedding model changes.
lessons.byHand: From a recorded week of document changes (edits, new pages, deletions, one renamed file), decide for each what the ingest job must do, then find why a deleted policy still shows up in answers.

units.title: Evaluation
units.about: Proving an LLM feature works and keeps working: test sets, retrieval and answer metrics, judges, error bars, regression checks, traces.

lessons.title: Golden sets: the test cases you write first
lessons.outcome: Build a small golden set from real user questions with expected answers and tags, and score a system against it.
lessons.byHand: From a pile of recorded real questions, drag 15 into the set so it covers the easy, the common and the nasty, and fill in the expected answer for each.

lessons.title: Retrieval metrics: recall@k, precision@k and MRR
lessons.outcome: Compute recall@k, precision@k and MRR for a retriever and say which number matters for a given product.
lessons.byHand: Score three recorded retrieval results by hand against the known relevant chunks, then predict which change (bigger k or a reranker) moves which metric.

lessons.title: Faithfulness: is the answer backed by the sources?
lessons.outcome: Check an answer claim by claim against its retrieved sources, score faithfulness separately from correctness, and add the checker to the RAG eval harness.
lessons.byHand: Split three recorded answers into single claims and mark each as supported, contradicted or not in the sources.

lessons.title: LLM-as-judge and its biases
lessons.outcome: Write a judge prompt with a rubric, check its agreement with human labels, and correct for position and length bias.
lessons.byHand: Label 12 recorded answer pairs yourself, then compare with the recorded judge verdicts, including the same pairs with the order swapped, and find where it disagrees.

lessons.title: Is a 2-point change real? Error bars by resampling
lessons.outcome: Put a bootstrap error bar on a golden-set score and decide whether a difference between two prompt versions is real or noise.
lessons.byHand: Click to draw ten resamples of 40 recorded pass/fail results, note each score, and decide from the spread whether 78 to 80 is a real gain.

lessons.title: Regression tests for prompts in CI
lessons.outcome: Run the golden set on every prompt change with noise-aware pass thresholds, and read a failing report to find the broken case; this lab starts the RAG eval harness.
lessons.byHand: Predict which golden cases a recorded prompt edit will break, then read the real before-and-after report and find the case that regressed.

lessons.title: Tracing LLM calls with Langfuse
lessons.outcome: Instrument a RAG or agent app with traces and spans, and use a trace to find the slow or wrong step.
lessons.byHand: Read a recorded trace tree of one slow, wrong answer and point to the span that caused it, before any code.

lessons.title: Error analysis: read the failures, count them, fix the biggest
lessons.outcome: Read a batch of failing traces, tag each with the step and kind of failure, count the tags, and pick the next improvement from the counts instead of from a hunch.
lessons.byHand: Tag forty recorded failing conversations (wrong retrieval, right sources but wrong answer, refused when it should answer, bad format, tool error), build the tally, and choose which single fix removes the most failures.

units.title: Agents
units.about: A model that picks its own next step: the loop, plans, memory, graphs, several agents, sign-off, failures and scoring runs.

lessons.title: The agent loop: think, call a tool, look, repeat
lessons.outcome: Write a minimal agent loop that calls tools until the model says it is done, with a hard step limit.
lessons.byHand: Play the model for a recorded support request: at each turn choose the next tool call from the tool list, then read the real tool result and decide whether to stop.

lessons.title: Agent or fixed workflow: choosing the right shape
lessons.outcome: Decide for a given task whether a fixed chain, a router, or a free agent loop fits, and justify it by cost and risk.
lessons.byHand: Sort six real feature requests into fixed chain, router or agent, then compare your choice with recorded step counts and failure rates for each shape.

lessons.title: Planning first, then acting, and replanning
lessons.outcome: Build a plan-then-execute agent that writes a step list, runs it, and replans when a step fails.
lessons.byHand: Order step cards into a plan for a multi-part request, then click the exact step in a recorded run where the plan went stale and pick the replan it needed.

lessons.title: Agent memory: scratchpad, session and long-term
lessons.outcome: Give an agent a working scratchpad and a long-term store, and choose what gets written to each.
lessons.byHand: Go through a recorded week of chats with one user and mark each fact as throwaway, keep for this session, or keep forever, then check what a recall query would return.

lessons.title: Agents as state machines in LangGraph
lessons.outcome: Model an agent as a LangGraph graph with typed state, nodes, conditional edges and a checkpointer; this lab starts the portfolio agent with tools.
lessons.byHand: Drag states and arrows into a refund-flow diagram in the page, then step a recorded run through your diagram and find the edge you forgot.

lessons.title: Human approval steps before risky actions
lessons.outcome: Pause the portfolio agent before an irreversible tool call, let a person approve or edit it, resume from the checkpoint, and say when sign-off only adds friction.
lessons.byHand: Tick which tool calls in a recorded agent run needed sign-off and which would only slow people down, then choose the fields the approval screen must show.

lessons.title: Letting an agent run code: sandboxes, CLIs and tool choice
lessons.outcome: Choose between a fixed tool, an MCP server, a command-line tool and a code-execution sandbox for an agent task, and list what the sandbox must block (network, files, time, memory).
lessons.byHand: For five recorded agent tasks pick the tool shape that fits, then read the run log of model-written code that tried to read files outside its folder and choose the sandbox rule that would have stopped it.

lessons.title: Several agents: supervisor, handoffs and their cost
lessons.outcome: Split a task between a supervisor and specialist agents, and tell when one agent with more tools would do better.
lessons.byHand: Read two recorded runs of the same task, one with a single agent and one with three, and count tokens, steps and where information got lost in each handoff.

lessons.title: Why agents fail: loops, wrong tools, made-up arguments
lessons.outcome: Diagnose the common agent failures from a trace and add the guard that stops each one.
lessons.byHand: Diagnose five recorded failing traces (a repeat loop, a wrong tool, an invented ID, an ignored error, an early stop) and name the fix for each before seeing ours.

lessons.title: Evaluating agents: outcome, path and cost
lessons.outcome: Trace the portfolio agent and score its runs on task success, tool-call correctness, step count and cost, and pick the metric that gates a release.
lessons.byHand: Grade ten recorded agent runs on success and on whether the path was acceptable, and find the run that succeeded the wrong way.

units.title: Context engineering
units.about: Deciding what goes into the model's window on every call, and keeping long conversations useful without overflowing it.

lessons.title: What goes in the window: a token budget
lessons.outcome: Split a context window into system, tools, retrieved text, history and room for the answer, and measure each part.
lessons.byHand: Given a recorded oversized request, count the tokens per section and choose what to cut so it fits while the answer stays right.

lessons.title: Long conversations: sliding windows and summaries
lessons.outcome: Implement a sliding window plus a running summary for chat history, and check which facts survive.
lessons.byHand: Read a recorded 60-turn chat, write the summary you would keep at turn 40, then check whether the bot's answer at turn 58 would still be right with it.

lessons.title: Compaction: shrinking an agent's context mid-task
lessons.outcome: Compact a long agent run by clearing old tool results and summarising, and tell when compaction loses something needed.
lessons.byHand: Mark in a recorded long agent trace which tool outputs can be dropped, which must stay word for word, and find the one dropped detail that broke the next step.

units.title: Fine-tuning
units.about: When changing the model's weights beats a better prompt or retrieval, and how to do it cheaply with a small, clean dataset.

lessons.title: Fine-tuning, RAG or a better prompt: choosing
lessons.outcome: Decide for a given failure whether a prompt change, retrieval or fine-tuning is the fix, and defend the choice.
lessons.byHand: Drag ten recorded assistant failures (missing facts, wrong tone, wrong label format, outdated catalogue) into prompt, RAG or fine-tune piles, then check against the answer key.

lessons.title: LoRA: training a small add-on instead of the model
lessons.outcome: Explain how LoRA adapts a frozen weight matrix with two thin matrices and build that update in NumPy.
lessons.byHand: Fill in the trainable-number count for a full 4096 by 4096 update and for a rank-8 pair, then predict the counts at rank 2 and rank 32 before the page checks them.

lessons.title: Building a dataset: real, synthetic and distilled
lessons.outcome: Assemble and clean a fine-tuning set from real messages plus teacher-model labels, and reject the rows that would teach the wrong thing.
lessons.byHand: Flag problems in twenty recorded training rows, some labelled by a larger teacher model: duplicates, contradicting labels, leaked test rows and confidently wrong teacher labels.

lessons.title: Fine-tune a small model with QLoRA
lessons.outcome: Run a QLoRA fine-tune on a free Colab GPU, apply the right chat template, and show the tuned model beats the base model on a held-out set.
lessons.byHand: Before training, predict for eight recorded held-out messages which team the base model will pick and where it breaks the label format, then compare with the tuned model's recorded answers.

units.title: Safety and guardrails
units.about: How LLM features get attacked or leak data, and the checks that sit between the model and anything it can touch.

lessons.title: Prompt injection through retrieved content
lessons.outcome: Explain why text a model reads can act as instructions and find the injected step in a recorded agent trace.
lessons.byHand: Click the exact line of a supplier's email in a recorded email-assistant trace that the model obeyed instead of the user.

lessons.title: Data leaks through agents: private data, untrusted text, a way out
lessons.outcome: Spot the three ingredients of an agent data leak (access to private data, exposure to untrusted text, a channel that can send data out) and break the chain by removing one of them.
lessons.byHand: Audit four recorded agent setups, mark which of the three ingredients each one has, and for the one that leaked choose the smallest change that makes the leak impossible rather than unlikely.

lessons.title: Jailbreaks and layered defences
lessons.outcome: Build a simple input screen, show where it fails against rephrased attacks, and choose which layers to add instead of a bigger blocklist.
lessons.byHand: For eight recorded attack prompts, tick which ones a given keyword rule would let through, then run your own filter to check the prediction.

lessons.title: Keeping personal data out of prompts and logs
lessons.outcome: Write a redactor that masks personal data before a prompt is sent or logged, and find the cases it misses.
lessons.byHand: Highlight every piece of personal data in ten recorded chats, then compare your highlights with what a pattern-based redactor caught.

lessons.title: Validating model output before it acts
lessons.outcome: Check model output against a schema and business rules, retry or refuse on failure, and know which checks belong outside the model.
lessons.byHand: Mark each of eight recorded refund proposals as execute, retry or send to a person after checking it against the schema and the refund policy.

units.title: Images, speech and documents
units.about: Getting photos, audio and scanned paperwork into an LLM system, and measuring where each conversion step loses information.

lessons.title: Sending images to a model
lessons.outcome: Prepare images so a vision-capable model reads them reliably, and tell when a plain OCR or rules step is the better tool.
lessons.byHand: Compare recorded model answers for the same receipt photographed blurred, tilted and cropped, and pick which preparation step fixes each wrong field.

lessons.title: Speech to text and word error rate
lessons.outcome: Transcribe audio with an open speech model, score it with word error rate, and know when a spoken reply via text-to-speech is not worth adding.
lessons.byHand: Align a recorded transcript with its reference and fill in the counts of substitutions, deletions and insertions to get the word error rate.

lessons.title: Parsing PDFs, tables and scans with OCR
lessons.outcome: Pick text-layer extraction or OCR for a document, find where tables and columns get scrambled, and fix the chunking that follows.
lessons.byHand: Compare a recorded text-layer extraction and an OCR output of the same scanned form and mark where table rows merged or two columns were read across.

units.title: Voice, computer-use and generative UI
units.about: Agents that talk, agents that click through screens, and model output that arrives as interface instead of text.

lessons.title: Voice agents: speech in, speech out, and the latency budget
lessons.outcome: Lay out a voice agent as speech-to-text, model, text-to-speech (or one speech-to-speech model), split its response time into a budget per stage, and handle interruptions and turn-taking.
lessons.byHand: Split a recorded slow voice reply into its stage timings, find which stage blows the budget, then choose fixes (streaming, a smaller model, earlier speech start) and see the new total.

lessons.title: Computer-use and browser agents
lessons.outcome: Explain how a computer-use agent works from screenshots and clicks, why it is slower and more fragile than an API, and when it is still the right choice.
lessons.byHand: Step through a recorded browser-agent run that fills in a supplier form, predict the next action from each screenshot, and find the step where it clicked the wrong button and why.

lessons.title: Generative UI: model output as components
lessons.outcome: Have a model choose and fill typed UI components instead of writing prose, validate the props before rendering, and decide when plain text is better.
lessons.byHand: Turn three recorded text answers into component calls (a table, a booking card, a chart), then find the recorded output whose props would crash the page and the schema rule that catches it.

units.title: Open models on your own hardware
units.about: Choosing an open model, fitting it in memory, and running it locally, for many users, and inside a closed network.

lessons.title: Choosing an open model
lessons.outcome: Shortlist open models for a job by licence, size, language ability and your own test results rather than leaderboard rank.
lessons.byHand: Fill a decision table for three candidate models from their recorded licence terms, sizes and scores on a small Korean test set, then pick one and name what would change your mind.

lessons.title: GPU memory and the KV cache: will it fit?
lessons.outcome: Explain what the KV cache stores per token and layer, and estimate weight plus cache memory to say which GPU or setting fits.
lessons.byHand: Fill in weight memory for a 7-billion-parameter model at 16 and 4 bits, then the KV cache per token and for one long conversation, before the calculator checks each cell.

lessons.title: Quantization: fewer bits per weight
lessons.outcome: Quantize weights to fewer bits in NumPy, measure the error it adds, and judge when the quality loss is too high for the task.
lessons.byHand: Fill a table rounding eight weights to sixteen 4-bit levels, then predict how one outlier weight changes the error for the rest of its group.

lessons.title: Running a model locally with Ollama
lessons.outcome: Run and call a quantized open model on your own machine and diagnose why a local run is slow or out of memory.
lessons.byHand: Read a recorded Ollama log and timing output and select the line that explains why one run is several times slower than another on the same laptop.

lessons.title: Serving many users with vLLM, even offline
lessons.outcome: Explain how batching and a paged KV cache let one GPU serve many users, tune a config from a load test, and list what an offline install must bring in.
lessons.byHand: Mark where a recorded load test of requests per second against latency saturates and pick the config line to blame, then tick each line of a recorded install log that reached the internet.

units.title: Working with coding agents
units.about: Coding agents end to end: how the harness works, planning before code, setup and safeguards, parallel runs, review, failure modes, memory and deployment.

lessons.title: Inside a coding agent: the harness around the model
lessons.outcome: Explain what the harness adds to the model (tools, codebase search, permission checks, context management, subagents) and trace one task through its tool calls.
lessons.byHand: Read a recorded coding-agent session as a list of tool calls, label each one (search, read, edit, run, ask), and predict when the context will run out and what the harness does then.

lessons.title: Writing a task a coding agent can finish
lessons.outcome: Write a coding-agent brief with scope, done criteria and a way to verify, and recognise tasks better done by hand.
lessons.byHand: Match three recorded agent runs to the three briefs that produced them, then rewrite the vaguest brief and choose which run it would have prevented.

lessons.title: Spec, plan, then code: steering an agent before it types
lessons.outcome: Turn a feature idea into a short spec and a step plan made of pieces that can each be checked, and review the plan before letting an agent execute it.
lessons.byHand: Reorder and split a recorded agent-made plan for a feature until every step has its own check, and find the step that silently assumed a database change nobody agreed to.

lessons.title: Instruction files and permissions for agents
lessons.outcome: Write a project instruction file and allow and deny permission rules that keep a coding agent inside the team's conventions and away from risky commands.
lessons.byHand: In a recorded agent session, mark the steps where it ran a destructive command or broke a team rule, then write the instruction lines and permission rules that would have stopped each.

lessons.title: Skills, hooks, MCP servers and plugins
lessons.outcome: Choose the right extension for a need: a standing instruction file, a skill that loads on demand, a hook that always runs, an MCP server that adds tools, or a plugin that bundles them.
lessons.byHand: Match six recorded team needs (always run the formatter, look up tickets, follow the release checklist, block edits to migrations, share the setup with the team, explain the codebase rules) to the extension that fits, then fix a hook that never fires.

lessons.title: How much to let an agent do alone: autonomy and safeguards
lessons.outcome: Pick an autonomy level for a task by its risk and how easy it is to undo, and set the permissions, sandbox and backups that make a mistake cheap.
lessons.byHand: Place eight recorded tasks on a grid of risk and reversibility, choose an autonomy level for each, then read a run where an agent deleted a folder and pick the safeguard that would have stopped it.

lessons.title: Running several coding agents at once
lessons.outcome: Split work so several agents can run in parallel without colliding: separate working copies, no shared files, a merge order, and a check on shared resources such as disk and test ports.
lessons.byHand: Given ten tasks and a recorded failed parallel run (two agents edited one file, one restored the other's backup, the disk filled), regroup the tasks into safe parallel batches and pick the checks to run before starting.

lessons.title: Reviewing and testing a coding agent's change
lessons.outcome: Find the typical faults in an agent-written change and write the tests that prove it works before merging.
lessons.byHand: Click the planted problems in a recorded agent diff (a deleted test, a swallowed error, a hard-coded key), then write the failing test cases for its date-parsing function before running them.

lessons.title: How coding agents go wrong
lessons.outcome: Recognise the common coding-agent failures (over-building, stopping short, claiming done without checking, risky file or data actions, drifting from the task) and the instruction or check that prevents each.
lessons.byHand: Diagnose six recorded agent transcripts, name the failure in each, and choose the one-line instruction or automatic check that would have caught it.

lessons.title: Agent memory across sessions, retros and cleanup
lessons.outcome: Keep what agents learn in standing context files and notes, run a short retrospective after a long run, and remove the duplicate code and dead files agents leave behind.
lessons.byHand: Sort fifteen recorded learnings from a long run into keep in the instruction file, keep as a note, or drop, then find the duplicated helper an agent added three times.

lessons.title: Agents in deployment and monitoring
lessons.outcome: Put agent work behind CI and human gates before release, and use an agent to read logs and alerts and propose a fix without giving it production write access.
lessons.byHand: Arrange the gates in a recorded release pipeline for agent-written changes, then read an agent's proposed fix from a log excerpt and decide whether to accept, ask for a test, or reject.

stages.name: Production
stages.end: Ship, monitor and pay for an AI product

units.title: Serving a model behind an API
units.about: Put an LLM feature behind a web endpoint that streams, survives slow calls and moves long work off the request.

lessons.title: A typed FastAPI endpoint around a model call
lessons.outcome: Write a FastAPI route with request and response models that wraps a model call and returns clean errors.
lessons.byHand: Given five recorded raw requests (one missing a field, one too long), decide by hand which the endpoint should accept, reject with 422, or cut down, then check against the schema.

lessons.title: Streaming tokens to the browser
lessons.outcome: Stream model output from a FastAPI route with server-sent events and parse a recorded event stream in browser JavaScript, including a dropped connection.
lessons.byHand: On a recorded token timeline, mark when the user first sees text with and without streaming, then find the spot in a recorded event stream where a proxy buffered everything.

lessons.title: Timeouts, retries and backoff for model calls
lessons.outcome: Choose timeout and retry settings for a model call and simulate backoff with jitter so retries do not pile up.
lessons.byHand: Replay a recorded log of failed provider calls and decide, call by call, which errors are worth retrying and which must fail fast.

lessons.title: Queues and background jobs for long AI work
lessons.outcome: Move slow or overnight bulk work onto a task queue with a job id, status polling, safe retries and batches sized for throughput.
lessons.byHand: Draw the timeline of a request that summarises forty contracts inline, mark where it times out, then redraw it with a queue and a worker.

units.title: Cost and latency
units.about: Measure what each request costs in time and tokens, then cut both with caching, budgets and routing.

lessons.title: Measuring latency percentiles and token cost
lessons.outcome: Compute p50, p95 and p99 latency and cost per request in token cost units from a request log, and say which number users actually feel.
lessons.byHand: Sort twenty recorded request times by hand, find the median and the slowest one in twenty, and predict which the average hides.

lessons.title: Choosing a hosted model, and mixing models
lessons.outcome: Choose a model for a feature from your own test set by plotting quality against cost and latency, and decide when to use different models for different steps.
lessons.byHand: Score five recorded models on the same twenty-question set, plot quality against cost and latency, pick the model for each of three steps of a pipeline, and explain why the leaderboard winner is not chosen.

lessons.title: Exact and semantic caching of answers
lessons.outcome: Build an exact-match cache and a similarity cache over embeddings, pick a safe threshold, and say how answer caching differs from prompt caching.
lessons.byHand: From a recorded list of real support questions, group by hand the ones that deserve the same answer, then find two that look alike but must not share one.

lessons.title: Token budgets and routing to cheaper models
lessons.outcome: Set per-request and per-user token budgets in cost units and route easy requests to a smaller model with a fallback to a larger one.
lessons.byHand: Label twenty recorded user requests as easy or hard by hand, then compare your labels with what a simple router decided and count its costly mistakes.

lessons.title: Distillation: teaching a small model from a big one
lessons.outcome: Explain how distillation trains a smaller model on a larger model's answers, when it cuts cost and latency enough to pay for itself, and how to check the student has not lost the hard cases.
lessons.byHand: Compare recorded teacher and student answers on an evaluation set, find the slice of hard cases where the student falls behind, and work out at what monthly volume the distilled model pays for its training.

units.title: Containers, clusters and cloud
units.about: Package the service so it runs the same everywhere, on CPU or GPU, and know what a cluster and a cloud platform add.

lessons.title: Packaging an AI service with Docker
lessons.outcome: Write a Dockerfile for a Python model service with pinned dependencies, a small image and model files kept out of the image layers.
lessons.byHand: Read a recorded build log and Dockerfile, predict which layers rebuild after a one-line code change, then reorder the file so they do not.

lessons.title: GPU containers and driver mismatches
lessons.outcome: Explain how a container reaches the host GPU and diagnose the common driver and CUDA version errors from their messages.
lessons.byHand: Match four recorded GPU error messages (captured on a cloud GPU, marked 'not run by us') to their cause: no runtime, driver too old, wrong CUDA build, out of memory.

lessons.title: Kubernetes in brief for model services
lessons.outcome: Read a Deployment, Service and autoscaler config for a model server and say what happens when traffic doubles or a pod crashes.
lessons.byHand: Given a config and traffic chart recorded on a local kind cluster, predict how many replicas run each hour and when a cold start would hurt users.

lessons.title: Hosted model APIs on a cloud platform
lessons.outcome: Call a cloud-hosted model API correctly: set up IAM auth, pick a region for data residency and read quota errors.
lessons.byHand: On a recorded config and error log (marked 'not run by us'), find why calls fail: wrong role, model not enabled in region, or quota hit.

lessons.title: Managed ML platforms versus self-hosting
lessons.outcome: Choose between a managed ML platform (SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML) and your own containers for a team's training and serving.
lessons.byHand: Sort six recorded team situations (fine-tuned open model, no ops staff, spiky traffic and so on) into managed or self-hosted, then defend one.

lessons.title: Ship the RAG service to a public URL
lessons.outcome: Deploy the containerised RAG and eval service with a small CPU model to a free no-card host, check its health endpoint and fix a failed deploy.
lessons.byHand: Work through a recorded failing deploy log line by line and point to the first line that explains the failure before reading the fix.

units.title: Tracking experiments, models and data
units.about: Record every run, promote models on purpose and version the data so any result can be reproduced months later.

lessons.title: Experiment tracking with MLflow
lessons.outcome: Log parameters, metrics and artefacts for training or prompt runs, compare them, and say when git tags and a sheet are enough.
lessons.byHand: Given a messy folder of recorded run notes and file names, try to answer 'which settings produced the best score' by hand and list what is missing.

lessons.title: A model registry and promoting versions
lessons.outcome: Register model versions, move one to production by alias, and roll back after a bad release.
lessons.byHand: From a recorded release history, work out which model version was live when a complaint came in and what rolling back would change.

lessons.title: Versioning datasets alongside code
lessons.outcome: Version a dataset next to the code that uses it so a past model can be retrained on exactly the data it saw.
lessons.byHand: Given two recorded dataset snapshots that differ by a handful of rows, find the changed rows by hand and explain why the model's score moved.

units.title: Monitoring, drift and feedback
units.about: Notice when a live AI feature gets worse, find why, and turn user feedback and labels into better data.

lessons.title: What to monitor in a live LLM feature
lessons.outcome: Choose the signals to log and alert on for an LLM feature (errors, latency, cost, refusals, quality samples) and set sane alert rules.
lessons.byHand: Look at a recorded week of dashboard charts and mark the one real incident among three false alarms, writing why each alarm fired.

lessons.title: Detecting input and quality drift
lessons.outcome: Compute a drift score between last month's and this week's inputs and decide whether it needs action.
lessons.byHand: Bin two recorded sets of question lengths and topics by hand, compare the histograms and predict whether quality will drop before running the numbers.

lessons.title: User feedback loops and their traps
lessons.outcome: Design a thumbs and corrections feedback flow, and spot when feedback is biased or the model is learning from its own outputs.
lessons.byHand: Go through recorded thumbs-up and thumbs-down events and find the pattern that makes the raw ratio lie (who votes, and when).

lessons.title: Labeling data and checking label agreement
lessons.outcome: Set up a small labeling task, measure agreement between two labelers and fix the guideline that causes disagreement.
lessons.byHand: Label twenty recorded customer messages yourself, compare with a second recorded labeler and compute how often you agree beyond chance.

lessons.title: A data pipeline from logs to a retraining set
lessons.outcome: Turn production logs into a cleaned, deduplicated dataset, reusing the personal-data redactor, ready for evaluation or fine-tuning.
lessons.byHand: Clean a recorded batch of fifty log rows by hand (duplicates, broken records), run the stage-5 redactor on it, and count the personal data it missed.

lessons.title: Incident response for an LLM feature
lessons.outcome: Run an incident for an LLM feature: detect it, stop the harm first (switch off, roll back the prompt, fall back to another provider), find the cause from traces, and write a blameless review.
lessons.byHand: Work through a recorded incident timeline (a prompt change that made a shopping assistant promise refunds, then a provider outage), choose the first action at each point, and write the one-sentence cause.

units.title: AI system design interviews
units.about: Practise designing whole AI systems out loud, from requirements to evaluation, in the interview format.

lessons.title: Mock interview: method and a support bot
lessons.outcome: Run an AI design answer in order (requirements, data, model, serving, evaluation, cost, failures) on a support bot with escalation.
lessons.byHand: Mark where a recorded weak answer skipped a step, then estimate daily volume, peak load and tokens per chat from a recorded traffic sample.

lessons.title: Mock interview: search over company documents
lessons.outcome: Design document search with permissions, freshness and citations, and explain how you would measure that it finds the right files.
lessons.byHand: Given a recorded set of documents with access rules, work out by hand which ones a given employee's answer may cite, and find the leak in a draft design.

lessons.title: Mock interview: a coding agent for a team
lessons.outcome: Design a coding agent with a sandbox, tool permissions, review gates and an evaluation set, and name how it fails.
lessons.byHand: Trace a recorded agent run that broke a build, mark the step where a guard should have stopped it, and choose which guard.

units.title: Finish and present the portfolio
units.about: Finish the RAG, agent and fine-tuning projects begun in stages 5 and 6, then write them up so a busy reviewer trusts them.

lessons.title: Finish the RAG project with its evaluation harness
lessons.outcome: Package the RAG repo built in stage 5 with its golden set, a baseline and a results table with error bars that reruns with one command.
lessons.byHand: Audit a recorded evaluation report from a sample RAG repo and flag each number a reviewer would distrust (12-question golden set, no baseline, hidden judge prompt) by choosing the flaw for each row.

lessons.title: Finish the agent project with tools and tracing
lessons.outcome: Ship the stage 5 agent so every run leaves a trace, and write up its three most common failures from those traces.
lessons.byHand: Sort five recorded traces of the agent into success, wrong tool, loop or bad answer, then pick the one-line fix that matches each failure type.

lessons.title: Finish the fine-tuned model served behind an API
lessons.outcome: Serve the small model fine-tuned in stage 5 behind the stage 6 HTTP endpoint and show with numbers whether it beat a prompted base model.
lessons.byHand: Tally recorded outputs of the prompted base model and the fine-tuned model on 40 held-out messages in a scoring grid, then decide whether the fine-tune earned its keep.

lessons.title: Write a README with its design decisions
lessons.outcome: Write a README that leads with the problem, a measured result and how to run it, followed by the main choices, the rejected options and why.
lessons.byHand: Reorder the blocks of a recorded weak README (setup steps first, no result, no system picture) into reviewer order, then for three of the RAG project's choices pick the rejected option and its reason.

units.title: Shaping the product
units.about: The product side of an AI engineer's job: from prototype to production, what a feature costs per user, testing it on real users, and explaining its limits.

lessons.title: From prototype to production: the build loop for an AI feature
lessons.outcome: Move an AI feature from a one-day prototype to an evaluated MVP to production in small steps, and decide at each step whether to gather user feedback, run an experiment or build more.
lessons.byHand: Order twelve recorded steps of a feature's life into prototype, MVP and production, mark the gate each must pass, and choose the next move at two decision points.

lessons.title: Unit economics of an AI feature
lessons.outcome: Work out what an AI feature costs per active user per month from tokens, calls and caching, compare it with what the user pays, and find the change that fixes a negative margin.
lessons.byHand: From recorded usage of a writing-assistant feature (calls per user, tokens per call, cache hit rate, a few heavy users), compute cost per user, find the margin, and pick between three fixes.

lessons.title: A/B testing an AI feature on real users
lessons.outcome: Design an online test for an AI change with one main metric and guardrail metrics, read the result with its uncertainty, and know when an offline evaluation is enough.
lessons.byHand: Pick the main and guardrail metrics for a recorded experiment, read its results table, and decide ship, roll back or keep running when the main metric rose but a guardrail fell.

lessons.title: Explaining what an AI feature can and cannot do
lessons.outcome: Explain an AI feature's error rate, failure cases and cost to non-engineers in plain terms, and turn a vague request into a feasible scope with a stated quality bar.
lessons.byHand: Rewrite three recorded engineer explanations for a sales lead, a lawyer and a finance manager, then answer 'can it be 100% accurate?' with numbers from an evaluation.

units.title: Job posts and interviews
units.about: Read what a posting really asks for, then practise concept, debugging and take-home rounds on recorded material.

lessons.title: Read an AI engineer job post and find your gaps
lessons.outcome: Split a job post into must-haves, nice-to-haves and filler, map each must-have to a lesson or project, and list the gaps to close first.
lessons.byHand: Tag each line of two invented composite postings, labelled as such (a hosted-model product team, and a Korean team running open models on-premise), as must-have, nice-to-have or filler, then score your fit.

lessons.title: Answer concept questions with a clear structure
lessons.outcome: Answer common AI engineer concept questions as definition, concrete example and trade-off, and handle the scenario follow-up that comes next.
lessons.byHand: For five questions (why RAG still makes things up, when to fine-tune, what LoRA changes, how to evaluate an agent, what temperature does), spot the flawed answer among three recorded ones and order the parts of a good one.

lessons.title: Diagnose a broken LLM system in a debugging round
lessons.outcome: Find the cause of a quality drop from a failing evaluation and a trace, state it in one sentence, and propose the smallest fix.
lessons.byHand: Work through a recorded failing evaluation and its traces, click the trace step where the answer goes wrong, and choose the cause: a changed chunk size that split every answer table in half.

lessons.title: Plan a take-home task inside its time box
lessons.outcome: Turn a take-home brief into a plan that fits the time box: what to build, how to evaluate it, and what to skip and say so.
lessons.byHand: For a four-hour brief to extract delivery dates and amounts from supplier emails, choose prompting or fine-tuning, drag the hours into a time budget, and pick the items for the 'what I would do next' list.
